chunks: He said: Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Babawayh - may God have mercy on him - reported from his father, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah ibn Mihran, from Abu al-Hasan Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon them both) who said - I heard him saying:
Do not regard your good deeds as too many, and do not consider your sins as too few, for indeed small sins accumulate until they become many.
And fear God, Mighty and Majestic, in private so that you treat yourselves with fairness.

And hasten toward obedience to God, and be truthful in speech, and fulfill the trusts, for indeed that is for your benefit. And do not engage in what is not permissible, for indeed that is against you.

key_terms.الأمانة: The trust, deposits or responsibilities entrusted to someone
key_terms.النصف: Fairness, justice, treating oneself equitably before God
key_terms.تستقلوا: To regard as too few or insignificant, to belittle
key_terms.تستكثروا: To regard as too many, to consider something excessive

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Musa al-Kadhim say about small sins accumulating?
ai.summary: Imam Musa al-Kadhim (AS) delivered this comprehensive moral exhortation to his followers, emphasizing a balanced spiritual outlook: never view one's good deeds as sufficient nor dismiss small sins, since minor transgressions accumulate over time. He then issued a series of practical commands - to maintain God-consciousness in private, hasten to obedience, speak truthfully, and return entrusted items - explaining that righteous deeds benefit the doer, while engaging in the forbidden brings harm upon oneself.
word_analysis: may He have mercy on him

en.mulla-asgharali-m-m-jaffer: 8. He said: Abu Ja’far Muhammad ibn ‘Ali ibnal-Husayn ibn Babawayh - may Allah have mercy on him, reported from his father, from ‘Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubaid, from Uthman ibn Isa from Sama’ah ibn Mehran, who said: I heard Abul Hasan Musa ibn Ja’far, peace be upon him, say:
"Do not regard your good deeds as too many, and do not consider your sins as too few. Surely, sometimes those little lapses gather together to become many.
And be mindful (fearful) of Allah, Most High, in your privacy, so that you are granted to treat yourselves justly.

And hasten towards obedience to Allah, and be truthful in your speech, and return the deposits held by you to the rightful owner. These traits are good for you; and do not get involved in things which are not legitimate for they will do you harm!"
